workstreams.title: Proof of concept — can an MCP server hand prompts to the client's model?
workstreams.body: Build the smallest possible test of the pure-oracle idea before any migration work starts. One MCP tool returns one assembled LAD prompt and its schema. Claude Code runs that prompt on the user's own model and posts the result back. The server makes no model call.

workstreams.title: Third proof of concept — small instructions that name local files, not embedded documents
workstreams.body: The second proof of concept failed. Zero of five runs were faithful. Two runs never started. The deep probe missed in every completed run. The assembled prompt was about 6,260 lines and sat at the Claude Code tool-result cap.

issues.title: Architecture tool runs on invented fixture documents instead of real LAD output
Guidance packs are hardcoded, so the layer-details document that selects them is never read
Brief fixture is Markdown, so the enhanced-else-original precedence is never exercised
Existing architecture is read from a fixture path, not from the monorepo root
featureName and the manifest are absent from the tool's inputs
The assembly gates pass without ever comparing the assembled text to the reference service's prompt
WS-3 measures a modified copy of the shipping setup prompt
